dataflowBytes.description:
DataflowBytes is this user's dataflow diagrams and every stored version of them.

🔴 It is NOT part of TotalBytes and NOT part of the quota, and that is permanent:
the quota is the object store's ledger, and diagram content lives in database rows
(master 2026-08-23, "只有 resource 才有这个限制"). Nothing else in this system can
see these bytes — neither the user's quota usage nor the instance total — so this
column is the only visibility they have.

⛔ Do not "fix" this by folding it into TotalBytes. That would silently turn a
deliberate exemption into a quota and start rejecting uploads for storage that was
promised not to count.

dataflowOverThreshold.description:
DataflowOverThreshold flags a user past dataflow.OwnerBytesWarnThreshold. There is
no retention policy behind it — nothing is deleted and no write is blocked. It
exists because the per-version cap limits how big one version is while nothing
limits how many versions there are.

quotaGB.description: Effective quota in GB (nil = unlimited for admins)

dataflowWarnThresholdBytes.description:
DataflowWarnThresholdBytes is the per-owner line DataflowOverThreshold is measured
against, sent so the page does not have to hardcode a number the backend owns.

totalDataflowBytes.description:
TotalDataflowBytes is the instance-wide diagram total, reported alongside
TotalBytes and never added into it — see StorageUsageEntry.DataflowBytes.

backend_available.description: Defaults to true if not specified

frontend_available.description: Defaults to true if not specified

api_key.description: Full key (only for user's own providers)

client_message_id.description:
ClientMessageID is the idempotency key: a client that retries a send it never got
an answer to reuses the id, and the server reports the earlier delivery instead of
writing the sentence twice. Optional — a client that does not retry may omit it and
the server mints one, which keeps the ledger's invariant (every delivery has a key)
without making every caller carry uuid machinery.

daemon_id.description:
DaemonID and DaemonName describe the machine the live session runs on, both empty
when nothing is running. The name is resolved here because the caller would
otherwise join it against a daemon list that may not contain the machine at all —
a session can outlive its daemon's visibility.

active_thread.description:
ActiveThread locates today's live thread — the task and root comment quick-input
clients (web modal, desktop panel, mobile sheet) preload recent context from and
navigate into. Nil when the user has never spoken to Alfred; POST /alfred/messages
opens the conversation on first send, so a client needs no create path of its own.

agent_user_id.description:
AgentUserID is the caller's OWN Alfred — the id an @mention link has to
carry to reach him.

It is here because the frontend used to hardcode the well-known UUID
00000000-…-ad07 (useFirstHandshake.ts) back when that named one Alfred for
the whole instance. Every user has their own copy under a fresh id now, so
a hardcoded constant addresses one person's Alfred and silently reaches
nobody for everyone else. Only the server can answer "which one is yours".

Empty when the caller has no copy yet — seeding is lazy — and a client must
treat that as "cannot mention him yet" rather than falling back to a
constant, which is the failure this field exists to remove.

conversation_task_id.description:
ConversationTaskID is the most recent chat this user has mirrored onto a task, or
empty when they have never sent a message. Most recent rather than a list: the card
offers one way in to the transcript, and the explorer is where someone browses the
rest.

ledger_task_id.description:
LedgerTaskID is the agent's home task — its long-term memory, in the task's notes.
Empty until the first session creates it, which is the normal state for a user who
has only just linked an account: the UI hides the entry rather than linking to a
task that does not exist.

provider.description: Provider is the messenger name, e.g. "telegram".

capabilities.description:
Capabilities names the optional API behaviours this build has, so a client can ask
instead of assume. See the Capability constants for the vocabulary.

frontend_url.description:
FrontendURL is the canonical base for links this server generates (share links,
invites). Electron needs it because its own origin is file://.

im_providers.description:
IMProviders lists the messengers a user can connect their own bot to on this server.
It is a statement about the build, not about any bot: under BYO bots there is no
instance-wide messenger connection to report on, and a bot's handle and health belong
to the user who registered it.

public_share_enabled.description: PublicShareEnabled reports whether the operator allows unauthenticated share links.

Selected permissions for this API key

timezone.description: Optional: defaults to "Asia/Shanghai" if not provided

accessToken.description: Success case: tokens and user info
Success case: tokens and user info

registration_enabled.description:
RegistrationEnabled reports whether this instance accepts self-service
signups. It rides on tier-info because that is already the public endpoint
the login page reads to learn what the instance allows — the alternative was
a second unauthenticated round trip saying one bool. The page uses it to
decide what to render; the backend still refuses on its own authority, so a
client working from a stale cache is wrong about the button, never about the
outcome.

returned byte for byte; decoding it into a map here would silently rewrite values

EntityType/EntityID attach the diagram to something as it is created — the same

stranded by a failed second request.

NotRollbackableReason is an error code (e.g. DATAFLOW_INLINE_DATA_URI), empty when

rollbackable.description:
Rollbackable says whether this version still satisfies the current content rules.
It is answered here, in the list, rather than when the button is pressed: people
reach for a rollback after something has gone wrong, and that is the worst moment
to hand them a surprise failure.

soul_owner_id.description:
SoulOwnerID / SoulOwnerName name the person who maintains this agent's soul
— its prompt, skills and defaults (agent.AgentConfig.OwnerID). Both are
empty on a human row.

"Who maintains it" is the fact a group needs about an agent that it does not
need about a person: an agent in a group is a thing other members may summon,
and its behaviour is whatever ONE person decides. Showing that person is what
makes the row accountable to someone.

The name is resolved from this same member list and nothing else (see
ToGroupMemberResponses). In v1 that always resolves, because the only way an
agent gets in is its own owner adding it while managing the group — so the
owner is a member by construction. If that ever stops holding, the name comes
back empty rather than wrong, and no new user-directory lookup was introduced
to make it resolve: this endpoint must not become a way to turn a uuid into a
name for a person you cannot already see.

type.description:
Type is "human" or "agent", and is the ONLY thing a client may branch on to
tell them apart. It is stated rather than inferable on purpose: what the UI
did before was guess — `username.includes('svc') || email.includes('@internal')`
— which reads an agent's INTERNAL KEY, the one thing C1 minted so that no
reader would ever have to. That guess also fails now by construction, since
this DTO drops an agent's email (see ToGroupMemberResponse), so the member
list would have rendered every agent as an ordinary person.

last_error.description:
LastError is the messenger's own words for the most recent failure, empty while
healthy. Safe for its owner to read: it describes their credential, never contains it.

state.description:
State is the supervision state of this bot's connection: "starting", "running",
"retrying" or "token_rejected". It is per-user, unlike the old instance-wide
provider state, because each user's bot fails and recovers on its own.

bot.description: Bot is null when the caller has not registered one.

cap_reached.description:
CapReached reports that the instance is at its limit of registered bots. Only
meaningful to a user who has none: replacing a token on an existing bot is always
allowed, since it adds no connection.

encryption_configured.description:
EncryptionConfigured reports whether this instance can store a token at all
(UD_ENCRYPTION_KEY). False replaces the whole section with an explanation.

multi_user_allowed.description:
MultiUserAllowed reports whether the IM access gate admits this user right now.
False for a non-owner while im.multi_user_enabled is off.

provider.description:
Provider defaults to telegram, the only messenger with an implementation today.
Present so a second messenger needs no new route.

token.description:
Token is the credential from @BotFather. Required. It is verified against the
messenger before anything is stored, and it is never returned by any endpoint.

expires_in_seconds.description:
ExpiresInSeconds saves the UI a clock comparison against a server timestamp, which
is the one thing a countdown must not get wrong on a device with a skewed clock.

monthlyCost.description:
MonthlyCost is the same burn rate over 30 days, rounded once from the unrounded
net cost. Always present; it is the fallback whenever subCent is true.

progress.description: Progress is nil when no expected life is set.

remainingDays.description: RemainingDays is nil when no expected life is set; 0 once the target is met.

residual.description:
Residual is straight-line book value for the trend chart ONLY.
It is not market value and must never be presented as net worth.

subCent.description:
SubCent is true when the real daily cost is non-zero but rounds to 0.00.
Clients MUST show monthlyCost instead of printing 0.00/day. Note dailyCost is
exactly 0 in this case, so scaling it client-side would just reproduce the lie.

belowPrecision.description: BelowPrecision marks a genuinely non-zero total that rounds to 0.00.

missingRates.description: MissingRates non-empty means this roll-up is INCOMPLETE and the UI must say so.

incomeAccountId.description: IncomeAccountID optionally records which account received the money.

recordIncome.description:
RecordIncome also books the proceeds as an Income. Ignored unless status is
"sold" with proceeds — giving something away or scrapping it earns nothing.

incomeId.description: IncomeID is empty when no income was requested or the disposal earned nothing.

FileSize is the exact byte length of the replacement. Confirm holds the upload to
this number — a short object is a failed upload, not a smaller file.

mimeType.description: MimeType is optional; the file keeps its current type when it is omitted.

currentFileKey.description:

wrote this comment on the reader-visible thread. Absent — the whole
object, not a false flag inside it — when a person wrote it or when an
agent wrote it for its own maintainer. Card 31881489 AC-2 is that absence,
which is why it is decided server-side and not by a frontend condition.
